name: Kish
description: Saul's father living at the time of United Monarchy

points: Now there was a man of Benjamin, whose name was Kish, the son of Abiel, the son of Zeror, the son of Bechorath, the son of Aphiah, a Benjamite, a mighty man of power.

Then the people said one to another, What is this that is come unto the son of Kish? That is like your big mama, your uncle, your friends. What happened to you? You have been celebrating Christmas your entire life. You love Christmas. What has happened to my baby? Who tricked you? You grew up in the Pentecostal church. What is wrong with Pastor Cleophus? They are saying, what have you turned into? What is this? And if they are not having that discussion, if they are not giving you that vibe, standoffish, it is because you have not fully changed into another man. You are still in a changing process, which is okay, but you must fully change into another man.

When they came to the hill, the company of prophets met him, and the Spirit of God came upon him, and he prophesied among them. The people that knew him beforetime said one to another, What is this that is come unto the son of Kish? and it became a proverb, Is Saul also among the prophets?

note.label: 1 Samuel 10: Saul Anointed Captain and Chosen King

points: When all the tribes came near, the tribe of Benjamin was taken, then the family of Matri, and Saul the son of Kish was taken; and when they sought him he could not be found, for the Lord answered, Behold, he hath hid himself among the stuff. They ran and fetched him thence, and when he stood among the people he was higher than any of the people from his shoulders and upward; he was real tall, taller than everybody.

note.label: 1 Samuel 10: Saul Anointed Captain and Chosen King

points: Jonathan's body had been hanged in the temple of Dagon, the fish god of the Hamites. David buried the bones of Saul and Jonathan in the country of Benjamin in Zelah, in the sepulchre of Kish his father, and performed all that the king commanded. After that the Most High was entreated for the land.

note.label: 2 Samuel 21: The Famine, the Gibeonites, and the Sons of the Giant

points: The chapter returns to Gibeon and repeats the line of Ner, Kish, and Saul, tracing Saul's sons and the house of Jonathan down through Micah to Azel.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 9: The Returned Inhabitants and Their Offices

points: And afterward they desired a king: and God gave unto them Saul the son of Cis, a man of the tribe of Benjamin, by the space of forty years. So this is who the Lord established, because of what we wanted. So even though we wanted a king, it was still the Lord that had to establish that.
